title: Marketplace Orders Buyer Return Terms
content:
**Terms.** A return may be requested only on a delivered Marketplace Orders order. Items in a non-returnable item category cannot be returned for a refund. The return is requested no later than the return window after the order is delivered. The window is the standard return window, or the renewed return window when the item was sold in renewed condition; the count starts the calendar day after the delivered date, each calendar day counts as one, and the request is in time on the last day of the window. When the option's holiday extension applies and the delivered date falls inside the holiday calendar's delivered-from to delivered-to range, the deadline is the later of the normal window end and the holiday return-by date of the following year. The returned quantity may not exceed the units ordered less units already covered by earlier return requests on the order. The return method must be one of the option's allowed return methods, or returnless when the returnless refund policy allows it.

## Eligibility, read from the order record

Each condition is read from the system record of the order the return is requested on, before the return is opened; a buyer's statement does not replace the record.

| Condition | Record that shows it | Met when |
|---|---|---|
| Order delivered | the order's status | the status is delivered |
| Category returnable | the order's item category | electronics, computers, apparel, shoes, home and kitchen, toys, beauty, large appliances or furniture (grocery is non-returnable) |
| Within the return window | the order's delivered date and the condition the item was sold in | the request date is no later than the last day of the window |
| Quantity available | earlier return requests on the order | the units requested do not exceed units ordered less units already covered |
| Method allowed | the option's allowed return methods | the method is one of them, or returnless where the returnless refund policy allows it |

## Counting the window

The clock starts from the event "the order is delivered", as shown by the delivered date on the order. Day one is the calendar day after the delivered date; the last day of a 30-day window is therefore the delivered date plus 30 calendar days, and a request on that last day is in time.

### Hypothetical boundary cases

| Delivered date (example) | Item sold as | Option's holiday extension | Last day to request | Request on the last day | Request the day after |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 10 March | new | not relevant (outside the holiday range) | 9 April | in time | late |
| 10 March | renewed | not relevant | 8 June | in time | late |
| 20 December | new | applies | 31 January of the following year (later than the normal end of 19 January) | in time | late |
| 20 December | renewed | applies | 20 March of the following year, or 19 March when February has 29 days (the normal end is later than 31 January) | in time | late |
| 20 December | new | does not apply | 19 January of the following year | in time | late |

The dates are example inputs on standard and renewed windows of 30 and 90 days and a holiday calendar running from 1 November to 31 December with a return-by date of 31 January.

### Quantity check, hypothetically

On a hypothetical order of 4 units with an earlier return request for 1 unit, a new request may cover at most 3 units.
